memos.headline: S04 and S06 Lead on Trend and Relative Strength; S02 in Freefall, S09 and S01 Lagging
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe as of May 2. S04 is the standout leader: +16.7% over 4 weeks, trading 12.5% above its 50-day and 5.1% above its 200-day mean, with 4w relative strength vs SPY of +11.1% and 12w of +11.5%—the best in the group. RSI at 72 is stretched, so I'd want to see a pullback toward the 50-day before adding, but the trend is unambiguously up. S06 is the cleanest intermediate-term chart: only -9.8% off its 52w high, above its 200-day mean by 7.9%, RSI 62, and low ATR of 2.47%—a steady uptrend with manageable volatility. On the other side, S02 is in a technical crash: RSI 25.7, -36% from its high, -26.6% below the 200-day, and -31.6% relative to SPY over 4 weeks—there is no sign of a bottom yet. S09 and S01 are both below their 50- and 200-day means with negative 4w relative strength, suggesting continued underperformance.

views.note: Strongest trend and relative strength in the universe; RSI 72 is hot so I'd buy a dip toward 400 (near 50d mean) and would reassess below 390.
Above both moving averages, shallow drawdown of -9.8%, low vol (ATR 2.47%), and positive 4w relative strength; would reconsider below 240 (200d area).
RSI 25.7 and -36% from highs with massive negative relative strength (-31.6% 4w vs SPY); no base forming yet, would need a close above 440 (near 50d) to reconsider.
Below both moving averages with -11.1% 4w relative strength vs SPY; would need a close above 110 (50d area) to turn neutral.
Negative 4w relative strength of -12.5% vs SPY, RSI 42, and trading below both key averages; needs to reclaim 168 (50d area) to improve.
Strong 4w bounce (+12.5%) but still -8.5% below 200d mean and -23.4% from highs; high ATR of 4.51% adds risk—watching for a sustained move above 120.
Middling RSI 48, below both averages, and negative relative strength; no catalyst in the chart to go either way until it clears 215 or breaks 195.
Decent 1w bounce (+5.6%) but still -9.5% below 200d mean and -22.4% from highs; needs to clear 340 to confirm trend reversal.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Show Best Earnings Power; S02 and S09 Margins Too Thin to Own
memos.body: I see the clearest durable earnings power in S10 (56.2% net margin, +77.9% YoY revenue growth, only $8.46B debt) and S05 (38.3% net margin, +46% YoY net income growth on $14.79B debt). S04 also impresses with 36.9% net margin and 13.3% revenue growth, though its $42.88B debt load warrants monitoring. On the other end, S02 at 5.5% net margin with $76.90B in total debt and S09 at 9.1% margin on declining revenue (-1.1% YoY) represent cash-flow compression risk I refuse to pay for. S06's $407.22B debt stack is eye-catching but its 32.3% margin and steady 8.1% revenue growth suggest a financial-sector balance sheet rather than distress; I'm neutral there pending further segment detail. The line items that would change my view are any margin compression at S10 or S05, or a meaningful revenue inflection at S09.

views.note: 56.2% net margin, near-80% revenue and earnings growth, and minimal $8.46B debt make this the strongest earnings-power story in the universe.
38.3% net margin with +46% YoY net income growth and a clean $14.79B debt load signals durable, expanding profitability.
36.9% net margin and 13.3% revenue growth are compelling, though $42.88B debt means I'd watch interest expense closely.
Revenue +10.5% and net income nearly doubling YoY are encouraging, but 10.7% net margin on $58B debt leaves limited margin of safety.
32.3% net margin is solid but $407B total debt (likely financial-sector) makes leverage assessment difficult without segment-level data.
29.2% net margin is healthy but revenue growth of only +4% YoY and $94.8B debt suggest mature, slower compounding.
19.1% margin is decent but -2.1% YoY revenue decline and $24.25B debt on a $19.78B revenue base give me pause.
Revenue declining -1.1% YoY with a thin 9.1% net margin and $36.76B debt signals cash-flow compression risk.
Only 5.5% net margin on $100.8B revenue with $76.9B debt and negligible +1.6% earnings growth is not a profile I want to own.
Revenue down -5.0% YoY with $31.74B debt nearly 2x annual revenue; margin expansion to 17.2% is encouraging but top-line shrinkage is a red flag.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 4.50% With Softening Growth Signals — Favor Duration-Sensitive and Defensive Names Over Cyclicals
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound has been unchanged at 4.50% for three months, yet the 12-month decline of 100 bp confirms the easing cycle is only suspended, not reversed. CPI running at +2.4% y/y is benign enough to keep cuts on the table, but unemployment ticking up to 4.2% (+30 bp y/y) signals a labor market that is cooling without cracking. The 10y yield at 4.33% has fallen 25 bp over three months while the 2s10s curve has steepened 19 bp to +0.55 pp, a classic early-slowdown configuration that rewards duration and penalizes late-cycle cyclicals. A hot April CPI print above +0.4% m/m or a payrolls surprise above 250k would challenge this slowdown call and push me back toward neutral on duration.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits from falling 10y yields and a steepening curve in a pause-to-easing regime.
Defensive staples outperform in a softening labor market with unemployment drifting higher and the Fed on hold.
Banks benefit from curve steepening (+19 bp in 3m) but face headwinds from slowing loan demand as unemployment rises.
Cyclicals look vulnerable as the labor market softens and the yield curve signals early slowdown rather than re-acceleration.
Energy typically underperforms in slowdown regimes; cooling demand backdrop and stable inflation reduce urgency for commodity exposure.
Rate-sensitive sectors gain as the 10y yield drops 25 bp over 3 months and the Fed signals patience before further easing.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: S04 Surges +7.6% While S02's -22.4% Crash Lingers
memos.body: I am reading the earnings-season price reactions as the clearest sentiment signal across this universe. S04 posted a +7.6% move on its 4/30 results, the strongest positive reaction in the group, suggesting a genuine narrative upgrade that may still have legs. S02's catastrophic -22.4% drop on 4/17 earnings followed by a board-level departure on 4/29 signals deeply negative sentiment that is unlikely to have fully cleared in two weeks. S08 just printed -3.7% on its 5/1 results, a fresh negative tone shift I want to avoid near-term. On the positive side, S06 rallied +4.0% on 4/11 earnings and has had steady filing activity since, suggesting constructive sentiment that has had time to consolidate rather than fade. S05 and S07 showed muted positive reactions (+1.7% and +0.6% respectively), which I read as neutral-to-slightly-positive tone with limited conviction either way.

views.note: A +7.6% earnings-day pop is the strongest positive sentiment signal in the universe and likely reflects a narrative upgrade still being digested.
A -22.4% earnings crash plus a subsequent officer departure signals deeply negative sentiment unlikely to reverse quickly.
Fresh -3.7% reaction to 5/1 earnings indicates negative tone shift still being absorbed by the market.
A +4.0% earnings pop on 4/11 with continued filing activity suggests constructive sentiment that has consolidated rather than faded.
A modest +1.7% earnings reaction and steady Other Events filings suggest stable but unremarkable sentiment.
A -3.7% earnings drop on 4/24 and no positive catalyst since leaves negative tone intact.
Muted +0.6% earnings reaction and two officer-change filings create an ambiguous sentiment picture.
No earnings reaction data and only governance/other filings leave me with no directional sentiment read.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty at Extreme Levels Signals Structural Geopolitical Risk Across the Universe
memos.body: I am seeing the most hostile policy backdrop in recent memory: the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index hit 890.82 on May 1, up nearly 248% over three months, while VIX sits at 24.60 (+50% over the same window). High-yield OAS has widened 110 bp in three months to 3.78%, confirming that credit markets are pricing real stress, not just headline noise. WTI crude at $60.59 (down ~17% in three months) suggests demand destruction fears or supply-side geopolitical shifts—possibly sanctions recalibration or OPEC+ policy changes—that weigh on energy-exposed names. I have moderate conviction that this is a structural shift rather than a one-quarter event; a clear de-escalation in trade/sanctions policy or a credible ceasefire framework would change my view. Filing activity across S05, S06, and S01 has been unusually heavy in April, which I read as companies proactively managing disclosure around policy-sensitive developments.

views.note: Four 8-K filings in six weeks suggest active management of policy-sensitive disclosures; I want to see content before taking a directional view.
Three 8-Ks in two weeks during peak uncertainty and widening HY spreads raise the risk of adverse policy exposure; staying away until clarity improves.
Heavy Reg FD and 8.01 filings in April suggest the company is navigating policy headwinds; the extreme uncertainty index keeps me sidelined.
Early-April disclosures coincided with the start of the uncertainty spike; with HY OAS up 110 bp in 3 months, credit-sensitive names face disproportionate risk.
Single mid-April 8-K gives limited signal; the macro backdrop of extreme policy uncertainty and falling oil prices warrants caution but not outright avoidance.
One Reg FD filing on April 10 is insufficient to form a strong view amid a 248% three-month surge in policy uncertainty.
Late-April Reg FD filing at least signals proactive communication; if the name has low direct trade/sanctions exposure, the steep VIX premium may offer opportunity, but conviction is low.
